question_text: During RAG evaluation, the retriever returns many chunks, but a large fraction are irrelevant to the question, diluting the context sent to the model. Which RAG evaluation metric specifically quantifies the proportion of retrieved context that is actually relevant?

options.text: Context precision — the ratio of relevant retrieved chunks to total retrieved chunks
Context recall — whether all relevant context was retrieved
Faithfulness — whether the answer is grounded in the context
Answer relevance — whether the answer addresses the question

explanation: Context precision measures how much of the retrieved context is relevant (relevant chunks ÷ total retrieved), directly capturing the 'too much irrelevant context' problem. Context recall measures whether all needed context was retrieved (a different failure — missing information). Faithfulness checks answer grounding; answer relevance checks question-answer alignment.

question_text: A RAG system frequently answers "I don't have enough information" even though the correct facts exist in the source corpus, because the retriever fails to surface the relevant passages. Which evaluation metric most directly measures this failure?

options.text: Context recall — whether all relevant context was actually retrieved (measured against a golden dataset)
Context precision — the fraction of retrieved context that is relevant
Retrieval latency — how fast the retrieval step is
Clarity — how well-organised the answer text is

explanation: Context recall measures whether the retriever surfaced all the relevant context that exists (typically compared against golden-dataset answers) — the exact failure when correct facts exist but are not retrieved. Context precision measures relevance of what WAS retrieved; retrieval latency is a speed metric; clarity concerns answer presentation.
